Hi Alex,

Wanted to understand how Redwood handles: per-token volume discounts, incremental commit tiers when adding new workloads, and any transition pricing for spikes during onboarding.

Can you share options for:

- How incremental commits stack with existing tiers (do they get blended rates?)
- Any recommended caps or protections for us while we evaluate model quality in prod

Appreciate a quick outline and a one-pager we can pass to procurement.

Thanks,

Hi Emma —

Thanks for the details and the usage estimates. Short answer: we can support a transitional "tier-bridge" approach that gives you predictable per-token economics during ramp and then folds the new workloads into a committed tier with a blended or stepped pricing depending on which you prefer.

Outline (high level):
- Bridge bucket (3 months): a temporary incremental bucket priced at a slightly higher discounted per-token rate than public list, but lower than on-demand. Purpose: predictable costs while you validate production quality.
- Incremental commit path: once you hit the agreed commit threshold (e.g., additional 1.0B tokens/month), we convert the bridge usage into a committed volume and apply the commit discount backdated for transition month.
- Blended vs step: we can do a blended reconciliation (average across old+new usage) or step tiers (new tokens priced at the new tier). Blended is simpler for accounting; step is sometimes more favorable long-term.
- Protections: soft caps + alerting, canary routing to lower-cost region/model, and an auto-fallback policy if quality/regression alerts trigger.

I'm attaching a quick spreadsheet that models a few scenarios (bridge length 1–3 months, blended vs step). See attached: bridge_pricing.xlsx

If that looks OK I can convert one scenario into a short-form proposal for procurement and include a DocuSign link.

Would you be available for a 30-min call Tuesday (4/13) or Thursday (4/15)?

Best,

Samir / Procurement team —

Attached is a short-form proposal (PDF) that reflects the recommended option:
- 3-month bridge bucket at $0.0009 per token (hosted API) for incremental usage up to 1.0B tokens/mo; bridge converts if sustained >= 1.0B tokens/mo for two consecutive months.
- Conversion option to a 9-month incremental commit at a blended rate of $0.00075/token (retroactive credit applied for the month of conversion, capped at 1 month).
- Unused committed tokens: 60% roll-forward (applied pro-rata the next billing month) + 40% forfeited. We can discuss a larger roll-forward window for enterprise deals.
- Protective guardrails: soft cap with pre-alert at 80% of bridge bucket, automatic canary routing, and a weekly quality checkpoint for 6 weeks.

Also included: DocuSign link to accept the short-form SOW and an outline of the SLA for Dedicated support during onboarding. Attachments: 2027-04-18-aceri-formal-proposal.pdf and the docusign pointer: 2027-04-18-aceri-docusign-link.txt

On the 9-month question: yes, we can offer a 9-month incremental commit rather than 12 months for the new volume — we added that into the SOW.

Let me know if procurement wants any specific invoicing cadence or additional acceptance criteria. Happy to hop on a quick call to run through the SOW.
